assertions.rationale: GO:0033862 is defined by the reaction ATP + UMP = ADP + UDP. Recombinant human CMPK2 (Q5EBM0), the orthologue named in the ISO/IEA 'with' field, was shown to phosphorylate dUMP, dCMP, CMP and UMP with ATP as phosphate donor, with kinetic parameters determined for each (Xu et al. 2008). UMP is the poorest of the four substrates, but the activity is a specific, kinetically characterised NMP-kinase reaction and so is not a marginal/nonspecific signal. The packet sequence is rat Cmpk2 (D3ZC63), the 1:1 orthologue of human CMPK2: in a pairwise global alignment I ran (Biopython PairwiseAligner, BLOSUM62) the two proteins are 74.0% identical over 443 aligned positions and 82.5% identical over the C-terminal nucleoside-monophosphate-kinase domain (human residues 250-449), with the P-loop motif conserved (rat GLDATGKTT / human GLDATGKTT). Conserved orthology plus a conserved catalytic domain supports transferring the measured activity to the rat protein.

Its efficacy to convert dUMP was highest, followed by dCMP, whereas CMP and UMP were the poorest substrates.' Abstract only; the JBC full text and PDF were not accessible to me (403).

I read only the abstract of Xu et al. 2008, so I did not see the UMP kcat/Km numbers; the abstract and UniProt both state UMP is a poor substrate. The GO definition cites EC 2.7.4.22 (bacterial-type UMP kinase), a different enzyme family, but the term is defined by the reaction, which CMPK2 catalyses.

assertions.rationale: Q86MW2 is Trypanosoma brucei MP67 = KREPB2, later renamed KREN3, one of the three RNase III-motif editing endonucleases of the ~20S editosome. Good experimental evidence exists that it is an RNA endonuclease: editosomes purified via tagged KREPB2 cleave a COII insertion-editing-site substrate at editing site 1, cleavage is lost when the RNase III-motif residues are substituted (E197V, D204A, E271A), and conditional repression abolishes COII editing in vivo. I confirmed by indexing the packet sequence that E197, D204 and E271 are present in the supplied protein. However, the requested term is defined mechanistically as 'two staggered cuts in both strands of dsRNA, leaving a 3' overhang of 2 nt'. The editing endonucleases make a single site-specific cut in the mRNA strand of an mRNA/gRNA duplex (one product mapping to a single editing site; the guide strand is not reported as cleaved), which is a related but distinct activity. The IEA source is also only a structural superfamily (IPR036389, RNase III endonuclease domain fold), which does not by itself establish the canonical double-strand staggered cleavage. Under the exact-definition rule the specific claim is not established.
sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2223309/ - Carnes J et al., Mol Cell Biol 2008 (PMID 17954557), 'RNA editing in Trypanosoma brucei requires three different editosomes': KREPB2 renamed KREN3; Fig. 5 (COIIcisU1/COIItransU1 cleavage by ~20S and TAP-purified editosomes; 'cleavage only occurs in editosomes that contain KREN3'); Fig. 6 (E197V, D204A, E271A abolish cleavage; D204A and E271A fail to rescue growth). Catalysis was assayed with purified editosomes, not with recombinant KREPB2 alone.

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1464856/ - Panigrahi AK et al., RNA 2006 (PMID 16611942): editosomes purified via KREN1, KREPB2 (TbMP67) and KREN2; KREN1 complexes cleave deletion sites, KREN2 complexes insertion sites; nuclease activity abolished by mutations in the putative RNase III catalytic domain.

https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR036389/ - InterPro description confirms IPR036389 is a homologous_superfamily (fold-level) entry.

assertions.limitations: This is a definition-match rejection, not a claim that the protein lacks endonuclease activity: KREN3/KREPB2 is well supported as the catalytic endonuclease subunit for COII insertion-site cleavage. If GO:0004525 is used by curators as a family-level term for RNase III-motif enzymes rather than strictly as written, the assertion would be acceptable (relation 'enables', since the catalytic residues are required). No study has reported the termini chemistry of KREN3 cleavage products directly, nor tested a canonical dsRNA substrate.

assertions.rationale: Mouse MED1 (Q925J9) is a Mediator complex subunit and a nuclear-receptor-binding coactivator; it has no known sequence-specific DNA-binding domain (its characterised DNA-contacting partners are LXXLL-motif-dependent nuclear receptors). I traced the ISO route: the rat source annotation (RGD:1559552 / D3ZRN2) is IDA from PMID 20702579, a chromatin-immunoprecipitation study of growth-hormone-responsive rat liver promoters, which shows Med1 occupancy at the Igf1 promoter. ChIP occupancy demonstrates that the protein is present at a cis-regulatory region; it does not show that MED1 itself binds a specific recognition sequence, and for a complex subunit recruited by DNA-binding activators the occupancy is expected to be indirect. The other mouse IDA DNA-binding annotations (PMID 15681609, PMID 18722179) are likewise promoter-occupancy/recruitment studies (PPARgamma-response element recruitment of coactivators; TFIID promoter occupancy), not direct DNA-sequence recognition. GO:1990841 (promoter-specific chromatin binding) rather than GO:0000978 is what such data support, and mouse Med1 already carries that term by IDA.

assertions.rationale: The only support is an InterPro IEA from the PgpA-domain entries (IPR007686 YutG/PgpA domain, IPR036681 PgpA-like superfamily), which are fold/domain-level entries that include uncharacterised proteins as well as genuine PgpA phosphatases. They conclude BT_1525 is most probably a phosphatidylinositol phosphate phosphatase. A phosphatidylglycerophosphate substrate was not tested, and no phosphatidylglycerophosphatase activity has been demonstrated for this protein, so the requested reaction (phosphatidylglycerophosphate + H2O = phosphatidylglycerol + phosphate) is not established.

assertions.rationale: The only support is a PANTHER/TreeGrafter IEA placing this sequence in PTHR36512 ('D-aminopeptidase'), i.e. family resemblance within peptidase clan S58 (DmpA/ArgJ fold). I aligned the packet sequence against NylC from the same strain (Q1EPR5, Agromyces sp. KY5R): the 306-residue packet protein matches NylC residues 50-355 at 99.0% identity, i.e. it is an N-terminally truncated NylC paralogue. The experimentally characterised activity of NylC is 6-aminohexanoate-oligomer endohydrolase (EC 3.5.1.117) - endo-type hydrolysis of amide bonds within nylon-6 oligomers, with Thr267 as the nucleophile generated by autoprocessing at Asn266/Thr267 and with Lys189/Tyr146 reported as nylon-specific catalytic/binding residues. That is not 'hydrolysis of a single N-terminal amino acid residue from a polypeptide chain', so the GO:0004177 definition is not matched. Two further problems weaken the attribution: UniProt records that this gene may not even be expressed (the 25 residues corresponding to NylC's N terminus are replaced by 76 residues derived from non-coding sequence and no plausible initiation codon lies in the replaced region), and the supplied sequence lacks the first 49 residues of the folded alpha subunit (NylC residues 1-266), so the autoprocessing-dependent active enzyme would probably not form.

assertions.rationale: O07118 is the Haloferax volcanii tRNA-splicing endonuclease (EndA, HVO_2952), an experimentally characterised enzyme. The native enzyme and recombinant protein expressed in E. coli cleave precursor tRNAs at the 5' and 3' splice sites, and substrate-recognition experiments with a series of mutant tRNA-Trp precursors and a 35-nucleotide model RNA showed that the enzyme requires a defined bulge-helix-bulge structure at the exon-intron boundaries and that these features alone are sufficient for recognition and cleavage. Specific, structure-dependent recognition and catalysis on an RNA substrate directly establishes binding to a nucleic acid, which is all GO:0003676 requires (RNA binding is a descendant of nucleic acid binding). The supplied 339-residue sequence is the same protein as the assayed one (UniProt O07118, H. volcanii DS2, taxon 309800 as given in the packet).

assertions.rationale: The single supporting annotation is an IBA from PANTHER node PTN000989481, whose cited reference proteins are human CANT1 (Q8WVQ1) and C. elegans apy-1. Both of those do hydrolyse GDP: recombinant human CANT1 has measured UDP > GDP >> ADP nucleotidase activity (EC 3.6.1.6, GDP + H2O = GMP + phosphate, RHEA:22156 - the exact GO:0004382 reaction), and C. elegans APY-1 depletion reduces membrane GDPase activity while heterologous expression in a yeast gda1 deletion raises it. However this PANTHER subfamily (PTHR13023:SF3) is not specificity-homogeneous: I checked that the arthropod salivary apyrases are in the same subfamily, and recombinant Phlebotomus duboscqi apyrase 'efficiently hydrolyzed ADP and ATP, but not AMP, GDP, CDP or UDP'. For the supplied Drosophila protein itself the one published measurement points to the arthropod-type specificity: CG5276 was shown to 'function as apyrases converting extracellular ATP to ADP and AMP', i.e. it has the ADPase activity that CANT1 essentially lacks. Sequence does not resolve the ambiguity: in my alignments CG5276 is 50.0% identical to human CANT1 and 49.3% identical to the Cimex lectularius apyrase. So a known functional difference inside the reference group blocks the inference, and GDP has never been tested on this protein.

assertions.rationale: The supplied 432-residue sequence is mycobacterial EgtA (GshA, Rv3704c and its identical orthologues in other members of the complex), a glutamate--cysteine ligase of the type 2 (EgtA) family. UniProt records the catalytic activity 'L-cysteine + L-glutamate + ATP = gamma-L-glutamyl-L-cysteine + ADP + phosphate' (EC 6.3.2.2, RHEA:13285) for this protein with experimental evidence (ECO:0000269) from Harth et al. 2005, in which each of the eight genes studied, gshA included, was expressed separately in M. smegmatis and the gene product assayed for enzymatic activity by analysing the reaction products. ATP is an obligate co-substrate of that ligation, consumed to ADP + phosphate, so demonstrated ATP-dependent ligase activity establishes that the protein binds ATP, which is all GO:0005524 requires. This is a very general term and the inference from an experimentally supported ATP-consuming catalytic activity to ATP binding is direct rather than family-level guesswork.

assertions.rationale: O80358 is Arabidopsis thaliana formamidopyrimidine-DNA glycosylase (AtFPG1/AthFpg, At1g52500), and the requested term, damaged DNA binding, has been shown directly on this protein. Duclos et al. (2012) determined the first crystal structure of a plant Fpg both unliganded and bound to DNA containing an abasic-site analogue (tetrahydrofuran); I confirmed in the RCSB records that PDB 3TWM is a protein/nucleic-acid complex (2 DNA entities) whereas 3TWK and 3TWL are protein-only, and all three map to O80358. An abasic site is a DNA lesion, so the co-crystal is a direct observation of this protein bound to damaged DNA. The same and earlier studies show lesion-specific glycosylase/AP-lyase catalysis on DNA containing FapyA, FapyG, guanidinohydantoin and spiroiminodihydantoin, which requires lesion recognition. assertions.rationale: The ISO source is human nicastrin (Q92542), where GO:0030674 rests on IMP/IGI work on gamma-secretase assembly. I checked the underlying biology rather than the single cited reference. Nicastrin is more than a passenger in the complex: in nicastrin-knockout mouse fibroblasts the Aph-1 to Pen-2 association is abolished and Aph-1 no longer co-precipitates the presenilin C-terminal fragment, and the nicastrin-Aph-1 subcomplex is required for the complex to associate with its substrate CTFbeta (no component co-precipitated CTFbeta in NCT-knockout or Aph-1-knockout cells). So removing this protein stops other macromolecules from being held together, which is what GO:0030674 describes - bringing two or more macromolecules into contact so they can act in a coordinated way - rather than mere complex membership. Transfer to the supplied rat Ncstn is safe: it is the 1:1 orthologue and in my alignment it is 88.8% identical to human nicastrin over essentially the full length (629/708 positions), with the same single-pass topology and large ectodomain.

assertions.rationale: P49067 is Pyrococcus furiosus AmyA (PF0272), and the protein was characterised directly. Laderman et al. purified the enzyme to homogeneity from P. furiosus and measured amylase activity: a homodimer of 66 kDa subunits, optimal activity near 100 C, no Ca2+ requirement, 'a broad range of substrate specificity, with the capacity to hydrolyze carbohydrates as simple as maltotriose'. assertions.limitations: Nothing has been published on NCU01209 itself (a Europe PMC search for the locus name returned no hits), so neither its DNA binding nor its target genes have been tested, and the specific gene set it regulates is unknown. The acceptance therefore depends on treating the intact Zn(2)Cys(6) module plus fungal TF C-terminal domain as a reliable functional rule; it does not establish which promoters are bound. Polymerase-II specificity is inferred from the fact that fungal nuclear protein-coding genes are transcribed by Pol II, not from an experiment.

assertions.rationale: The support is a single IBA whose reference protein is C. elegans zyg-12 (WBGene00006997), which does have direct evidence of dynein light-intermediate-chain binding (GO:0051959 by IPI from PMIDs 14697201 and 19635841). But zyg-12 is a Hook-family protein - UniProt Q23529, entry name HOOK_CAEEL, PANTHER subfamily PTHR18947:SF39 - whereas the supplied protein is zebrafish Daple/ccdc88c in subfamily PTHR18947:SF31. PANTHER family PTHR18947 ('CCDC88/GRDN G-protein modulator') lumps the Hook adaptors and the CCDC88/girdin signalling scaffolds, which share only the N-terminal Hook/calponin-homology module; the light-intermediate-chain-binding element of Hook adaptors lies in the coiled-coil region just after that module and is not known to be present in CCDC88 proteins, whose characterised functions are G-protein and Dishevelled-linked signalling. The nearest relevant experimental data are against the specific claim: in the human dynein interactome screen, Daple (CCDC88C) appeared in the intermediate-chain IC2 BioID dataset, not the LIC1 dataset (girdin/CCDC88A was the LIC1 hit), both Daple and girdin co-immunoprecipitated dynein and dynactin as whole complexes, and neither conclusively activated dynein/dynactin motility. Co-precipitating the dynein holocomplex, or proximity to the intermediate chain, does not establish binding to the light intermediate chain, which is what GO:0051959 requires.

assertions.limitations: This is an 'insufficient support' call. CCDC88 proteins do associate with dynein/dynactin, so light-intermediate-chain binding is not excluded; it simply has not been demonstrated, and the cross-subfamily PANTHER inference from a Hook protein is not strong enough on its own. I read the Redwine et al. text through an automated page read covering roughly the first 100,000 characters, so later supplementary tables were not checked, and I did not read the zyg-12 primary papers beyond their GO records.

assertions.rationale: The ISO chain leads to human ANK2, whose GO:0019901 annotation is an IPI with obscurin (UniProtKB:Q5VST9) from Cunha & Mohler 2008. Obscurin is a genuine protein kinase - UniProt lists Q5VST9 as 'Obscurin (EC 2.7.11.1) ... Obscurin-myosin light chain kinase', with keywords Kinase and Serine/threonine-protein kinase, and InterPro finds two complete protein kinase domains (IPR000719/PF00069, two occurrences) - so binding it satisfies the GO:0019901 definition of binding to a protein kinase. The interaction evidence is strong and mapped rather than a single pull-down: ankyrin-B and obscurin co-localise at the myocyte M-line and co-immunoprecipitate from heart; the interaction was localised to a novel exon 43' and two motifs in the ankyrin-B regulatory domain, both of which are required; a GFP-regulatory-domain construct acts as a dominant negative by competing for obscurin at the M-line; and the human R1788W variant adjacent to the obscurin-binding motif increases obscurin binding. The authors state that the exon-43'-containing transcript is the primary cardiac isoform in human and mouse, and the co-immunoprecipitation was from heart. Transfer to the supplied mouse Ank2 is safe: it is 84.6% identical to human ANK2 over 3887 aligned positions in my alignment.
sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2581558/ (PMID 18782775) - Cunha SR, Mohler PJ, J Biol Chem 2008, 'Obscurin targets ankyrin-B and protein phosphatase 2A to the cardiac M-line' (abstract read): exon 43' mediates obscurin interaction; two required motifs; co-IP from heart; dominant-negative competition; R1788W increases obscurin binding.

https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/services/annotation/search?geneProductId=UniProtKB:Q01484&goId=GO:0019901 - human ANK2 'enables GO:0019901', IPI, PMID:18782775, with UniProtKB:Q5VST9, assigned by BHF-UCL.

https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/search?query=accession:Q5VST9 - Obscurin, EC 2.7.11.1, keywords include Kinase and Serine/threonine-protein kinase; https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/all/protein/uniprot/Q5VST9/ shows two IPR000719 protein kinase domains.
Sequence comparison performed locally by me: packet mouse Q8C8R3 vs human Q01484 FASTA from UniProt, Biopython PairwiseAligner/BLOSUM62, 3287/3887 = 84.6% identity.
assertions.limitations: The GO term is satisfied because the interaction partner happens to be a kinase; the mapped binding site is in obscurin's non-kinase region, so the annotation says nothing about kinase-domain recognition or about regulation of kinase activity. I read the abstract of the primary paper rather than its figures. The ankyrin-B isoform question matters in principle (the obscurin-binding exon 43' is alternatively spliced), and I did not verify which isoform the 3898-residue packet sequence corresponds to; the authors report that the exon-43' isoform predominates in mouse heart.

assertions.rationale: P13498 is p22phox (CYBA), the alpha/light subunit of flavocytochrome b558. The holoenzyme is a haemoprotein, but the haems belong to the other subunit. The cryo-EM structure of the human NOX2 core complex shows the NOX2 (gp91phox) transmembrane domain forming 'an hourglass-shaped scaffold that sandwiches two heme groups orthogonal to the membrane plane', with 'Conserved histidine residues on TM3 and TM5 coordinate the hemes (His101, His115, His209, His222)' - all four ligands on NOX2. p22 is described as a four-helix transmembrane fold (TM1-TM4) and is given no haem-coordinating residue and no cofactor. The packet's sole support is an InterPro IEA from IPR007732, whose own description states that flavocytochrome b558 'is a heterodimer that consists of a large glycoprotein gp91phox ... (beta subunit) and a small protein p22phox (alpha subunit)'; the GO:0020037 mapping on that family entry therefore reflects a property of the complex, and specifically of the partner subunit, rather than of p22phox. Nothing I found attributes haem binding to p22phox itself, so 'enables heme binding' is not supported.
sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9568551/ (PMID 36241643) - Noreng S et al., 2022, 'Structure of the core human NADPH oxidase NOX2': quoted sentences on the hourglass-shaped NOX2 scaffold sandwiching the two haems and on the coordinating histidines His101, His115, His209, His222 on NOX2 TM3/TM5; p22 described as a four-transmembrane fold with no cofactor assigned.

https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR007732/ - 'Cytochrome b558 alpha-subunit' family description, which assigns the haem-containing catalytic core to the heterodimer and distinguishes gp91phox (beta) from p22phox (alpha).
https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P13498 - human CYBA, 195 aa, cytochrome b-245 light chain (record consulted for identity of the packet sequence).
assertions.limitations: p22phox is genuinely required for the maturation and stability of flavocytochrome b558, and loss of p22phox abolishes the cytochrome b558 spectrum in cells, so an argument could be made for a 'contributes_to' relation to haem binding by the complex. I did not find structural or biochemical evidence that p22phox contacts haem, which such a relation would need, and the asserted relation here is 'enables'. The automated read of the structure paper covered roughly the first 100,000 characters, so I did not inspect every supplementary statement about p22 ligands.
